option_relations.rationale: Lobular capillary hemangioma is a benign vascular proliferation, while Angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular tumor. They are distinct entities.
Tufted angioma is a benign vascular tumor, whereas Angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular tumor. Despite both being vascular lesions, they are fundamentally different in their biological behavior.
Acquired tufted angioma is a benign vascular tumor, while Angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular tumor. They are distinct in their nature and prognosis.
Microvenular hemangioma is a benign vascular tumor, whereas Angiosarcoma is a malignant vascular tumor. There is no direct clinical relationship between these two diagnoses.
